text:
zoe: heads up — onboarding q8-int8 variant of the bert-qa family and the eval-runner CI smoke shows weird metric divergence. pass@1 increased ~6pts vs fp16 but BLEU and BERTScore dropped across the board. CI job: eval-smoke/quant/2349998770 failed on metric assertions. Anyone seen an artifact like this?

matt: hmm, that usually smells like dedup/normalization mismatch between generator and metric pipeline. can you paste the runner logs? :thinking_face: 

zoe: logs excerpt below (already redacted model ids):
```
INFO generated: 5 candidates
INFO dedupe kept: 5
INFO pass_at_1: 0.54
METRIC BLEU: 0.32
METRIC BERTSCORE: P:0.68 R:0.71 F:0.69
ASSERT pass_at_1 >= baseline (0.48) -> OK
ASSERT BLEU >= baseline (0.40) -> FAIL
```
Looks like pass@1 is higher but BLEU lower. the runner's dedupe step prints "kept: 5" which is suspicious.

jia: i ran a tiny repro locally with the quantized build — found lots of invisible unicode variants in candidates (non-breaking spaces, zero-width joiners) so the naive dedupe that does strip().lower() misses duplicates. quantized tokenization sometimes emits NBSP for spaces between punctuation.

eval-bot: CI failure detail: eval-smoke/quant/2349998770
```
AssertionError: metrics mismatch
  expected BLEU >= 0.40 but got 0.32
  pass_at_1 reported 0.54 but recalculated (post-normalize) 0.46
```

luis: that explains inflation — if dedupe is operating on different normalization than the metric code (which runs its own normalizer before BLEU/BERTScore) pass@k will count duplicates as unique candidates. suggestion: unify normalization function used by generator/dedupe/metrics. simple NFKC + whitespace collapse fixed a local test for me.

matt: can you share the current dedupe snippet? maybe it's brittle. 

zoe: current dedupe in runner (simplified):
```
seen = set()
unique = []
for c in candidates:
    t = c['text'].strip().lower()
    if t in seen:
        continue
    seen.add(t)
    unique.append(c)
```
This is obviously too naive.

luis: new normalize proposal:
```
import unicodedata, re

def normalize_text(s):
    s = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", s)
    s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s)
    return s.strip()
```
use normalize_text both before dedupe and inside metric scoring. add a smoke unit that asserts pass_at_k computed on raw vs normalized doesn't diverge by >0.05.

nadeem: also check that tokenizers used in generation and in the metric pipeline are the same model/tokenizer version. quantized builds sometimes get a tokenizer mismatch patch when the wheel build pulls an older tokenizer. we should assert tokenizer.version equality in the smoke.

sre-bot: Canary job started: build/runner-canary/2349998775 for branch feat/quant-onboard-normalize - logs -> https://ci.redwood.internal/build/2349998775

z o e: typo in my previous msg, meant to ping @matt — i'll open the PR with the normalize_text change + unit + CI assert. assigning to @matt for review. :white_check_mark: 

matt: thanks — will review. also add a quick dashboard snapshot link in the PR showing before/after metric curves so PMs can see the regression.

zoe: created PR: https://git.redwood.internal/r/redwood/eval-runner/pulls/3421 — includes normalization, tokenizer-version check, and a new smoke test that fails CI if pass@k and BLEU diverge beyond the tolerance. leaving notes for release highlights.

nadeem: we should also add an integration test that runs quantized model generation against a golden set to catch tokenizer drift. i'll take that as a follow-up.

matt: re: dashboards — i've queued a manual rerun on the shared job to regenerate the dashboard tiles after the canary completes. will post results.

zoe: thanks all. keeping this open until canary passes and PR is merged. 

sre-bot: Canary job finished: build/runner-canary/2349998775 - status: SUCCESS (logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/build/2349998775/console)

zoe: can confirm after merge + re-run the inflated pass@1 went down to expected ~0.46 and BLEU recovered to 0.41. closing this thread but capturing learnings in the onboarding checklist (normalize + tokenizer-version assertion). :tada:
